_meta.purpose: One row per built interactive, so a new build can be checked against the fleet before anyone writes a new widget. Read by scripts/widget_pipeline/match_existing_widgets.py.

fields.targets: the misconception the widget exists to falsify
fields.also_fits: families where the same idea is taught - a reuse hint, never proof
fields.reuse: portable = drop it in as it stands; variant_needed = the mechanism carries but the deck names one context, so a new deck behind ctx.variant is required; content_bound = the widget IS one named case
fields.after: the MAP anchor - the strip is inserted BEFORE the heading whose text starts with this string; '$end' appends after the last section

_meta.maintenance: Add a row here whenever a widget is built, in the same commit as the build. Families follow FAMILY_RULES in match_existing_widgets.py.
_meta.family_rules_note: A subject slug maps to one family; see FAMILY_RULES in match_existing_widgets.py.

widgets.name: Name the behaviour
widgets.targets: Active listening is demonstrated through six distinct, nameable behaviours, each signalling something specific to the speaker.
widgets.teaches: Active listening is six distinct, nameable behaviours, each doing a different job for the speaker.

widgets.name: ADSR — the shape of one note
widgets.targets: Attack, decay, sustain and release interact simultaneously to shape a sound's evolving envelope, rather than being four separate consecutive events.
widgets.teaches: Attack, decay and release are times; sustain is the level held while the key is down. The four act together on one note.

widgets.name: What happens next?
widgets.targets: Antibodies tag, clump or neutralise pathogens; phagocytes/other cells do the actual destroying.
widgets.teaches: Antibodies bind to one matching antigen and tag, clump or neutralise the pathogen; phagocytes do the destroying, and antibiotics are drugs that kill bacteria only.

widgets.name: The Armada’s chain of disaster
widgets.targets: The Armada failed through a chain of geographic and logistical consequences, not because a storm blew up out of nowhere: the storm is the last link in the chain, not the cause.
widgets.teaches: The Armada was destroyed by a chain of geographic and logistical consequences — no deep-water port, an exposed anchorage, fireships, cut anchor cables, storm coasts — with the storm last in the chain, not first.
widgets.reuse_note: The chain is the 1588 Armada itself. Only fits a lesson on that campaign.

widgets.name: The gold foil experiment
widgets.targets: An atom is not a solid, densely packed ball, it consists of a tiny dense nucleus surrounded by mostly empty space occupied by electrons.
widgets.teaches: An atom is mostly empty space: a tiny, dense nucleus about 10 000 times smaller than the atom carries nearly all the mass.

wired_lessons.after: Models as Tools: Strengths and Limitations

widgets.name: Inside a bending part
widgets.targets: Bending a material creates simultaneous tension on one face and compression on the opposite face, not a single bending force.
widgets.teaches: Bending is not one force: the part curves, so one face is pulled longer (tension) while the opposite face is squashed shorter (compression), at the same moment — and which face is which flips with the supports.

widgets.name: Trace the binary search
widgets.targets: The halving strategy of binary search depends on the list being sorted; on unsorted data it cannot reliably locate items.
widgets.teaches: Binary search halves the list by checking the middle item; the discard is only safe because the list is sorted, so on unsorted data the search can throw away the half holding the target.

widgets.name: Where the food goes
widgets.targets: Most biomass/energy loss between trophic levels is due to respiration (heat loss from movement/life processes), not simply parts of organisms being uneaten.
widgets.teaches: Respiration, not undigested material, is the biggest loss of biomass between trophic levels; only about a tenth is passed on.

widgets.name: Energy in, energy out
widgets.targets: Bond breaking and bond making are simultaneous/overlapping parts of one process, and it's the relative energy stored in bonds (not timing) that determines exothermic vs endothermic.
widgets.teaches: Breaking bonds takes energy in and forming bonds gives energy out; the balance of the two totals decides exothermic or endothermic, not which happens first.

widgets.name: Where the lines cross
widgets.targets: The break-even point and subsequent profit/loss are determined by the relative positions and slopes of the cost and revenue lines, not simply the point where losses stop.
widgets.teaches: Break-even is the crossing of the total revenue and total cost lines; contribution sets the gap, and costs or price move the crossing.
widgets.reuse_note: Business scenarios are generic (no named firm), so another board's break-even lesson needs no new data.

widgets.name: Collisions that count
widgets.targets: Increasing temperature increases the proportion of particles with energy above the activation energy (shifting the distribution), which matters more than simply increasing collision frequency.
widgets.teaches: Warming a reaction shifts the whole spread of particle energies, so the share of collisions above the activation energy rises far more than the collision count does; a catalyst lowers the barrier instead, and concentration only adds collisions.

wired_lessons.after: Core Practical — Measuring Rates of Reaction

widgets.name: Follow the energy
widgets.targets: Wasted thermal energy is transferred to the surroundings and becomes increasingly spread out (dispersed), but it still exists — it is not destroyed or lost from the universe.
widgets.teaches: Wasted energy is transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings and dispersed, never destroyed or used up; the total always balances, and efficiency is the useful share of it.

widgets.name: Two scenes, one cut
widgets.targets: Cross-cutting forces an audience to hold two simultaneous narrative realities in tension, serving a structural/thematic purpose beyond preventing boredom.
widgets.teaches: Cross-cutting is a structural choice: the meaning lives in the juxtaposition, not inside either scene.
widgets.reuse_note: Scene material is original and neutral - no published play is quoted.

widgets.name: Where does the current go?
widgets.targets: Current is the same everywhere in a series circuit; it is energy/voltage that is shared out across components according to their resistance, not current disappearing.
widgets.teaches: Current is the same at every point in a series circuit: charge flows in a closed loop and is not used up. Components differ because they take different shares of the potential difference.

widgets.name: Movement or shift?
widgets.targets: A change in the good’s own price causes a movement ALONG the existing demand or supply curve; only a non-price factor (incomes, tastes, costs, technology, taxes) shifts the whole curve to a new position. "Demand increases when price falls" confuses the two: quantity demanded changes, the curve itself has not moved. One widget must serve both curves — treat demand and supply as data for the same mechanism.
widgets.teaches: A change in the good’s own price moves the point along the demand or supply curve; only a non-price factor shifts the whole curve.

wired_lessons.after: Factors That Shift the Supply Curve

widgets.name: Movement or shift?
widgets.targets: A change in price causes a movement along the existing demand curve, while only non-price factors cause the whole curve to shift.
widgets.teaches: A change in the good’s own price moves the point along the demand curve; only non-price factors shift the whole curve.
widgets.reuse_note: SUPERSEDED by curve-movement-vs-shift (which covers supply too) and wired to no lesson. Prefer the newer file.

widgets.name: Remove one condition
widgets.targets: Dependent origination is a simultaneous, interconnected web of conditions arising together, not a simple linear chain of causes.
widgets.teaches: Dependent origination is a web of mutually conditioning factors, not a one-way chain: remove a condition and everything resting on it ceases, while its own conditions carry on.

wired_lessons.after: The Five Aggregates in Everyday Life

widgets.name: Devolution: who decides?
widgets.targets: Devolved nations have specific powers granted by and still ultimately subject to the central government, unlike fully independent countries which have complete sovereign control over their own affairs.
widgets.teaches: Devolution transfers a named, unequal list of powers to the Scottish Parliament, the Senedd and the Northern Ireland Assembly; reserved matters and legal sovereignty stay with the UK Parliament.

widgets.name: Across the spectrum
widgets.targets: The seven regions of the EM spectrum are not fundamentally different things but a single continuous spectrum differing only in wavelength/frequency.
widgets.teaches: The seven named regions are labels on one continuous slide of wavelength and frequency; in a vacuum every EM wave is transverse and travels at 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

widgets.name: Sealed flask: the next ten seconds
widgets.targets: At equilibrium, forward and reverse reactions both continue at equal rates simultaneously — the reaction hasn't stopped and concentrations need not be equal
widgets.teaches: At equilibrium both reactions carry on at equal rates, so the amounts hold steady — steady, not equal.

widgets.name: Which stage changes what?
widgets.targets: In the fetch-execute cycle, decoding is a simultaneous interpretation of the fetched instruction rather than a separate sequential step in time.
widgets.teaches: Decode is the control unit interpreting the instruction just fetched. It writes to no register: fetch moves the instruction into the CPU, execute moves the data.

widgets.name: Reading a field map
widgets.targets: Electric field lines are a visual map of field strength and force direction, not physical objects or the literal path a charge follows
widgets.teaches: Field lines map the direction of the force on a positive charge, and their spacing maps the strength. They are not rails, and the space between them is not empty.

wired_lessons.after: Uses and Dangers of Static Electricity
Uses and Hazards of Static Electricity

widgets.name: Grade the shot
widgets.targets: Colour choices in cinematography are a deliberate narrative/thematic tool, not incidental decoration.
widgets.teaches: The colour of a shot is a storytelling choice, not a record of how the place happened to look. Each palette makes a claim about where we are and what we should feel, so the same shapes mean different things under different colours.
widgets.reuse_note: Every round is written around Skyfall, a set film. Another board or another set product needs a new round deck behind ctx.variant.

wired_lessons.after: Typicality: Blockbuster Aesthetic as Analytical Question

widgets.name: Up the fractionating column
widgets.targets: Fractional distillation separates hydrocarbons by differences in boiling point (vapour condensing at different heights/temperatures), not by physical sieving of molecule sizes.
widgets.teaches: Each hydrocarbon in crude oil condenses at the height where the column temperature first falls below its own boiling point, so high boiling points collect low down.

widgets.name: Which starch reaction?
widgets.targets: Gelatinisation needs water and thickens, while dextrinisation is a dry heat browning reaction of starch — they are not the same process.
widgets.teaches: Gelatinisation needs water and heat and thickens a liquid; dextrinisation is dry heat and browns a surface.

widgets.name: Where does the infrared go?
widgets.targets: Greenhouse gas molecules absorb infrared radiation and re-emit it randomly in all directions, with some returning to Earth's surface, rather than heat being physically trapped or blocked.
widgets.teaches: Greenhouse gas molecules absorb outgoing infrared and re-emit it in random directions within a fraction of a second, so about half returns to the surface. Nothing is trapped.

wired_lessons.after: Effects on People and the Environment
Key Greenhouse Gases and Their Sources
Climate Models and the Role of Evidence

widgets.name: Half-life: how much is left?
widgets.targets: Half-life is the time for half of the remaining nuclei to decay each time (never reaching zero), producing an exponential decay curve, not a countdown to total decay.
widgets.teaches: Each half-life halves the remaining nuclei, so decay is exponential and never reaches zero.

widgets.name: One beat, two loops
widgets.targets: The left and right sides of the heart contract simultaneously (not sequentially), pumping blood through two connected loops, with the left ventricle wall thicker to generate higher pressure for the systemic circuit.
widgets.teaches: Both sides of the heart contract on the same beat, driving two circuits at once, so blood passes through the heart twice on each lap of the body.

wired_lessons.after: The Cardiac Cycle: How the Heart Beats

widgets.name: Carrier or affected?
widgets.targets: A single dominant allele is enough to prevent a recessive disorder showing, so a carrier (Ff) is unaffected despite carrying the recessive allele.
widgets.teaches: One working allele is enough: a heterozygous carrier of a recessive disorder has no symptoms at all, yet can still pass the faulty allele on.

widgets.name: Defending the Holderness coast
widgets.targets: Protecting one stretch of coast with hard defences can starve neighbouring areas of sediment and increase erosion there, so 'protecting the coast' is not uniform or consequence-free.
widgets.teaches: Hard defences hold the stretch they stand on, but by trapping the drift or cutting off the cliffs that feed it they starve the beaches downdrift, where erosion then speeds up.
widgets.reuse_note: The stretch modelled is Holderness. A board that teaches a different coastal case study needs its own cell data behind ctx.variant.

wired_lessons.after: Soft Engineering: Working With the Sea

widgets.name: What Iago actually does
widgets.targets: Iago succeeds not through clever rhetoric alone but by exploiting the gap between what characters actually do and how others interpret those actions
widgets.teaches: Iago works on the gap between what people do and what it looks like: he arranges sights, strips context, moves real objects and refuses to finish sentences, then lets the other man draw the conclusion.
widgets.reuse_note: Built on nine moments of Othello. Only fits an Othello lesson.

widgets.name: Read the rock backwards
widgets.targets: Crystal size in an igneous rock is direct EVIDENCE of cooling rate: slow cooling deep underground grows large crystals; fast cooling at the surface freezes small ones; two-stage cooling gives porphyritic texture. The misconception is that coarse/fine are mere descriptive labels, or that crystal size depends on "how much time the magma had" in some vague sense disconnected from depth and setting. The rock is a thermometer you can read backwards.
widgets.teaches: Crystal size records cooling rate: slow cooling deep underground grows large crystals, fast cooling at the surface freezes tiny ones, and two crystal sizes mean two cooling stages.

widgets.name: Who feels a rate change, and when
widgets.targets: Interest rate changes propagate unevenly and with time lags depending on mortgage type and decision-making, not uniformly and instantly to everyone
widgets.teaches: A base rate change reaches households and firms unevenly and with different lags: variable borrowers and savers within weeks, fixed deals only when the term ends, firms and renters gradually over months.

widgets.name: Where do the ions go?
widgets.targets: In electrolysis, ions move because opposite charges attract at a distance, not because electrodes 'pull' ions or ions move randomly.
widgets.teaches: In electrolysis the ions themselves migrate: positive ions to the negative cathode where they gain electrons, negative ions to the positive anode where they lose them.

widgets.name: Kenilworth Castle: reading the plan
widgets.targets: Kenilworth's location, water defences and building phases work together as one unified military and aesthetic system, not as a static fortress read about in isolation.
widgets.teaches: Kenilworth as one spatial system: outcrop, mere and building phases answering each other, defence giving way to display.
widgets.reuse_note: A plan of Kenilworth Castle. Only fits the Kenilworth historic environment option.

wired_lessons.after: Robert Dudley and the 1575 Royal Visit

widgets.name: What the label does next
widgets.targets: A label is not just a name given once — it is a self-reinforcing process: the label changes how others treat the person, which narrows their options, which pushes them towards the behaviour the label predicted (master status → self-fulfilling prophecy → deviant career). The misconception is that a label is a passive description rather than an active mechanism with stages that each do causal work.
widgets.teaches: A label is a self-reinforcing chain — reaction, closed doors, master status, self-fulfilling prophecy — not a passive description.

widgets.name: Where the loss stops
widgets.targets: Limited liability means an owner's personal assets are protected if the business fails, but it does not stop the business itself going bust or guarantee no loss
widgets.teaches: Limited liability draws a legal line around the owner’s own things: the company still owes every penny it owes, and the owner still loses what they put in — the loss is capped, not cancelled. A sole trader has no such line.

widgets.name: Longshore drift: the pebble’s path
widgets.targets: Longshore drift results from swash moving sediment up-beach at an angle and backwash pulling it straight back, causing a zigzag net movement along the coast.
widgets.teaches: Swash carries sediment up the beach on the wave bearing, backwash drains straight back down under gravity, so each wave shifts the sediment along the coast in a zigzag.

wired_lessons.after: Erosional Landforms: Headlands, Bays, Cliffs & Stacks
UK Case Study: The Holderness Coast

widgets.name: Change one P, test the mix
widgets.targets: Changing one of the four Ps creates knock-on pressure on the others, so they must be adjusted coherently together.
widgets.teaches: The four Ps are one joined-up decision: change one and the others come under pressure, and the test of a mix is whether all four still point at the same target market.

wired_lessons.after: The Integrated Marketing Mix and Competitive Advantage

widgets.name: Same afternoon, two bulletins
widgets.targets: Different outlets covering the same event construct competing versions of reality through selection and combination, rather than simply reporting neutral facts.
widgets.teaches: Two accurate bulletins can leave audiences with different versions of one event, because each is built by selection, order and wording rather than simply shown.
widgets.reuse_note: The event is invented and outlet-neutral (Bulletin A / B), so it carries to any board's media language or news lesson.

widgets.name: Four hormones, one loop
widgets.targets: Multiple hormones (oestrogen, LH, FSH, progesterone) rise, fall, and trigger/suppress each other simultaneously through feedback loops, rather than acting in a simple day-by-day sequence.
widgets.teaches: The menstrual cycle as overlapping hormone curves driving each other by feedback, not four separate stages in a list.

wired_lessons.after: When Organs and Control Systems Fail

widgets.name: Blocked routes, five adaptations
widgets.targets: Merton's five responses to strain are structural adaptations to blocked goals available to anyone in that position, not fixed personal choices or character traits.
widgets.teaches: Merton’s five responses to strain are structural adaptations to blocked goals, not personality types.

widgets.name: Spin, orbit and the face we see
widgets.targets: The Moon does spin on its axis, but its rotation period exactly matches its orbital period around Earth, which is why we always see the same face — it is not stationary/non-rotating.
widgets.teaches: The Moon rotates once per orbit (both about 27.3 days), so the same face stays towards Earth; a Moon that did not spin at all would turn every side towards us.

widgets.name: Four kinds of movement
widgets.targets: The four motion types (rotary, linear, reciprocating, oscillating) must be distinguished by how they actually move over time, not just by static description, especially reciprocating vs oscillating.
widgets.teaches: Rotary, linear, reciprocating and oscillating motion told apart by the path a point traces, and the mechanisms that convert one into another

widgets.name: Same substance, smaller pieces
widgets.targets: Nanoparticle properties don't scale down predictably with size—there's a threshold where surface-area-to-volume ratio becomes large enough to dominate behaviour
widgets.teaches: Cutting a solid adds no material but converts inside into surface: total surface area rises by the number of divisions per edge, so surface-area-to-volume ratio climbs as pieces shrink. In the 1-100 nm range so much of the substance is surface that it behaves unlike the bulk.

wired_lessons.after: Properties That Change at the Nanoscale

widgets.name: What happens to the population?
widgets.targets: Variation already exists before selection; organisms don't consciously try to adapt or gain traits because they are needed, and 'fittest' means best suited to environment, not strongest.
widgets.teaches: Variation exists first by random mutation; the environment only selects among the variants already present, and populations shift while individuals do not.

widgets.name: The road to 30 January 1933
widgets.targets: The Nazis' rise depended on specific contingent events (Depression, political miscalculation) rather than being an inevitable result of ideology or charisma
widgets.teaches: The Nazi rise was contingent: the vote was falling before Hitler was appointed, and no free election gave the party a majority.
widgets.reuse_note: Germany 1918-33. Portable across boards that teach that period, nowhere else.

wired_lessons.after: Bruning and the Politics of Austerity
The Appeal of Hitler and the Nazi Party

widgets.name: Negative feedback: predict what happens next
widgets.targets: Negative feedback loops continuously correct deviations around a setpoint and switch off once corrected, repeating as needed, rather than being a single one-off correction.
widgets.teaches: Negative feedback corrects continuously around a set point, overshoots slightly, and never switches off for good.

widgets.name: Name the partner force
widgets.targets: Newton's third law action-reaction pairs act on two different objects and never cancel each other out; they cannot explain why one object stays still
widgets.teaches: A Newton’s third law pair is the same type, equal in size and opposite in direction, with one force on each of two different objects — which is why a pair never cancels.

widgets.name: Where the organelles actually sit
widgets.targets: Organelles occupy a coordinated, densely packed 3D arrangement in the cytoplasm where position/proximity matters, rather than floating randomly
widgets.teaches: Organelles are packed into a crowded arrangement in which position serves the cell’s job, not scattered at random through empty cytoplasm.

widgets.name: Reactivity down a group
widgets.targets: Reactivity increases down Group 1 (easier to lose an electron) but decreases down Group 7 (harder to gain an electron) — the trends are opposite, not the same rule.
widgets.teaches: Reactivity rises down Group 1 and falls down Group 7, because the same growing atom makes an outer electron easier to lose and an incoming one harder to gain.

widgets.name: What sets the rate?
widgets.targets: When a photosynthesis graph plateaus, one factor has become limiting while others are still present in excess — nothing has 'run out' or stopped working
widgets.teaches: A plateau means one factor has become limiting while the plotted factor keeps rising; raise the limiting factor and the whole plateau lifts.

wired_lessons.after: Resources That Producers Need: Minerals and Water

widgets.name: Predict what the child says
widgets.targets: Each Piagetian stage represents a fundamentally different, more sophisticated way of reasoning about the world, not simply a set of age-linked facts to memorise.
widgets.teaches: Piaget’s stages are qualitatively different ways of reasoning, not age labels or amounts of cleverness.

wired_lessons.after: Piaget and Inhelder’s Three Mountains Task (1956)
The Core Study: Piaget (1952) and the Conservation of Number

widgets.name: Story order, screen order
widgets.targets: Story is the full chronological sequence of events in the fictional world; plot is the order and selection of events actually shown to the audience, which can differ from story order.
widgets.teaches: Story is every event in the film world in chronological order; plot is what the film selects and the order it shows it in.
widgets.reuse_note: Mini-narratives are original; no real film is used.

widgets.name: From monomer to repeat unit
widgets.targets: When a C=C double bond opens during polymerisation, its electrons are used to form new single bonds with neighbouring carbons, not lost or 'broken off'.
widgets.teaches: In addition polymerisation the C=C opens: one of its two bonds breaks and those electrons form the single bonds joining monomer to monomer, so no atoms are lost and nothing is added.

wired_lessons.after: Alkenes — The Monomers for Addition Polymers

widgets.name: Will the water get through?
widgets.targets: Porosity measures how much space (pores) a rock has, while permeability measures how well those pores are connected to allow fluid flow through them, so high porosity does not guarantee high permeability
widgets.teaches: Porosity is how much pore space a rock holds; permeability is whether that space is connected and wide enough for water to flow. High porosity does not guarantee high permeability.

widgets.name: The post-production schedule
widgets.targets: Post-production involves multiple specialists working simultaneously on different tasks, not a single linear editing stage.
widgets.teaches: Post-production runs several specialists in parallel off shared versions; picture lock is the point the picture stops moving, and a re-cut after it forces sound, colour, graphics and music to re-conform.

widgets.name: Two numbers, one month
widgets.targets: A recorded sale/profit does not mean cash is immediately available to pay bills; profit and cash flow are different measures.
widgets.teaches: Profit and cash are different measures on different clocks: trade credit separates the sale from the money, so a profitable month can end overdrawn.

widgets.name: Reading a Punnett square
widgets.targets: Each cell in a Punnett square represents a distinct, equally likely combination of alleles from the two parents meeting, not just a lookup answer.
widgets.teaches: Each cell is one equally likely pairing of one gamete from each parent, so the ratio is a probability at every fertilisation, not a prediction of four actual offspring.

wired_lessons.after: Codominance and ABO Blood Groups (Triple Only)

widgets.name: Which way do the electrons go?
widgets.targets: Displacement reactions occur because more reactive metals more readily lose electrons to less reactive metal ions — position in the reactivity series reflects and explains this electron-transfer tendency, not physical force or arbitrary memorisation.
widgets.teaches: A metal’s place in the reactivity series is how readily it loses electrons, which is why a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its compound.

wired_lessons.after: Reactions with Water and Dilute Acid

widgets.name: Where do the lines land?
widgets.targets: Redshift arises because the wavelength of light is lengthened as the source recedes or as space expands, not because the light itself is being pulled or stretched like a rubber band by the galaxy.
widgets.teaches: Redshift is the arriving wavelength being stretched because the source recedes: faster recession gives a bigger shift, and the biggest shifts belong to the most distant galaxies.

widgets.name: Where does the steel go?
widgets.targets: Reinforced concrete works because steel bars are positioned within the concrete to resist tension, not simply bonded to its surface.
widgets.teaches: Steel sits where the concrete is being stretched — low in a sagging beam, high over a cantilever support — and it is buried inside the concrete, not fixed to its surface.

widgets.name: Combining forces on one line
widgets.targets: Forces in opposite directions subtract (vector combination) rather than just adding magnitudes together.
widgets.teaches: Forces are vectors: forces in opposite directions subtract and forces in the same direction add, and only a non-zero resultant changes the motion.

wired_lessons.after: Newton’s Second Law and F = ma
Weight, Mass and Gravitational Field Strength

widgets.name: Can it live on its surface alone?
widgets.targets: Surface area to volume ratio is a real physical constraint on diffusion rate, not just an abstract number, and explains why larger organisms need specialised exchange systems.
widgets.teaches: Volume outgrows surface area, so SA:V falls as size rises — the physical reason large organisms need exchange surfaces.

widgets.name: Sampling a sound wave
widgets.targets: Digital sampling involves the ADC repeatedly measuring wave height at fixed intervals; missing intervals loses information, it isn't a single one-off action.
widgets.teaches: Sampling is repeated measurement at fixed intervals: the stored file is rate × bit depth × seconds, and the wave between the measurements is lost.

widgets.name: Where Do the Volts Go?
widgets.targets: In a series circuit the current is the same everywhere; it is the supply voltage that divides between the components, in proportion to their resistance.
widgets.teaches: In series the current is identical everywhere, and the supply voltage divides between components in proportion to their resistance
widgets.reuse_note: One of the three hand-built house widgets (js/lesson-widgets.js lineage). Overlaps current-not-used-up - pick one per lesson.

widgets.name: Filling the texture
widgets.targets: A small number of instruments/voices can combine to fill a texture that sounds full and orchestral, without needing many players.
widgets.teaches: A small ensemble sounds full when its parts cover the range from bass to treble and each part does a different job — melody, countermelody, inner harmony, bass line. Adding players who double what is already there adds loudness, not fullness.
widgets.reuse_note: Register model only - no set work is named, so any board's ensemble or texture lesson fits.

widgets.name: Sonata form: follow the keys
widgets.targets: Sonata form requires the second subject to modulate to a related key in the exposition, distinguishing it from simple 'theme repeated' structures
widgets.teaches: Sonata form is defined by its key scheme: the second subject modulates away in the exposition and returns in the tonic at the recapitulation.
widgets.reuse_note: Keys are computed by semitone arithmetic from any home key, so it carries to every board's structure lesson without new data.

widgets.name: What does this storage actually stop?
widgets.targets: Food, moisture, warmth and time interact to enable microbial growth (e.g. warmth only matters with moisture present), rather than acting independently.
widgets.teaches: Microorganisms need nutrients, moisture, warmth, oxygen and a suitable pH together, so a storage method stops spoilage only where it shuts a condition off completely; a condition merely held down buys time and nothing more.

widgets.name: Where does the energy go?
widgets.targets: During a change of state, energy continues to be absorbed/released (breaking/forming bonds) even though the thermometer reading stays flat.
widgets.teaches: While a substance is changing state the supplied energy goes to the potential store, overcoming the forces between particles, so the average kinetic energy — and the temperature — holds steady.

wired_lessons.after: Changes of State and Specific Latent Heat

widgets.name: Choosing a stratified sample
widgets.targets: Stratification divides a population into groups first; a separate method (random/systematic) is then used to actually sample within those groups
widgets.teaches: Stratification only divides the population into groups and fixes each group’s share of the sample; a random method must still choose the individuals inside every group.
widgets.reuse_note: Populations are a school, a gym, a hospital, a college, a club. A geography fieldwork deck (transects, quadrats) would read better there, but the widget is correct as it stands.

widgets.name: Trace the load path
widgets.targets: Different structural systems (e.g. load-bearing walls vs frames) carry weight differently, so removing a wall carries different risk depending on the system.
widgets.teaches: Load-bearing (cellular) walls carry the building down through the walls themselves, while a frame carries it on columns and beams and leaves the walls between as infill that can be opened up.

wired_lessons.after: Superstructure: Frame, Upper Floors and Roof Supports

widgets.name: Follow the slab down
widgets.targets: A subducting plate descends at a shallow angle while remaining in contact with the overriding plate, rather than sinking straight down like a stone in water.
widgets.teaches: A subducting plate descends at a shallow angle and stays in contact, so the trench, the deepening earthquake foci and the volcanic arc all sit where the slab’s path puts them.

widgets.name: How far does the signal get?
widgets.targets: At a synapse the electrical impulse triggers neurotransmitter release across the gap, which then generates a new electrical impulse in the next neuron, it does not simply jump across like a spark.
widgets.teaches: At a synapse the electrical impulse stops at the gap; neurotransmitter is released, diffuses across and binds to receptor molecules, and only then does a new electrical impulse start.

widgets.name: The two scoreboards
widgets.targets: Battlefield success and strategic victory are different scoreboards. Each side has its own victory condition and often a clock: Germany’s 1918 Spring Offensive gained more ground than any attack since 1914 yet failed strategically because it did not achieve a decisive result before American strength arrived — and the gains left long, indefensible lines. US search-and-destroy in Vietnam won engagements and body counts, yet the NLF’s condition was to NOT LOSE until American political will broke. The widget must make the two scoreboards concrete: the tactical metric can climb while the strategic position worsens. Build once — the two wars are scenario data for the same mechanism.
widgets.teaches: Battlefield success and strategic victory are separate scoreboards: each side has its own war aim and its own clock, so the tactical count can climb while the strategic position gets worse.
widgets.reuse_note: The only widget that implements ctx.variant: decks 'ww1' and 'vietnam'. A third conflict means a third deck, not a new widget.

wired_lessons.after: Chemical Weapons: Agent Orange and Napalm

widgets.name: Theatre spaces: where does the audience sit?
widgets.targets: Different stage configurations (thrust, in-the-round, proscenium etc.) are not interchangeable room layouts — each imposes different constraints on blocking, design and audience relationship.
widgets.teaches: Each staging configuration is a different performer-audience contract, not a seating variant: the number of sides decides what can be built, where an actor can stand, and who sees the back.

widgets.name: Chains that slide, or a net that holds
widgets.targets: Thermoforming polymers soften reversibly when heated and can be remoulded, while thermosetting polymers undergo permanent cross-linking and cannot be reshaped once set — they behave fundamentally differently when heated.
widgets.teaches: A thermoforming polymer is separate tangled chains that slide when heated, so it softens and re-shapes again and again. A thermosetting polymer is one cross-linked network, so it never softens: heat only chars it.

widgets.name: How the tholos stands up
widgets.targets: The tholos tomb is a large engineered structure with a long approach and corbelled stone construction built into a hillside, not a simple underground chamber
widgets.teaches: A Mycenaean tholos tomb is an engineered corbelled structure, not a cave or a heap: each ring oversails the last, a capstone closes the span, and the mound loads the dome into stability.
widgets.reuse_note: A Mycenaean tholos tomb. Fits the Mycenaean world only.

widgets.name: High tide at Whitby
widgets.targets: The Moon does not pull ocean water towards it like a magnet making ONE bulge. Tidal force is DIFFERENTIAL gravity: the near side is pulled more than Earth’s centre, and Earth’s centre more than the far side — so water piles up on BOTH sides, and a coastline rotating through both bulges gets two high tides a day, roughly 12½ hours apart. The far-side bulge is the part the misconception cannot explain and the widget must make inevitable.
widgets.teaches: Tidal force is the difference in the Moon’s pull across Earth: the near side is pulled hardest, the centre less, the far side least. Water stands high at both ends, so a coast meets a high tide about every 12 hours 25 minutes.

widgets.name: Timbre: same notes, different music
widgets.targets: Timbre is an integral part of compositional meaning chosen alongside melody and harmony, not a decorative addition applied afterward.
widgets.teaches: Timbre is chosen alongside the notes, not added afterwards: the same pitches change meaning depending on which instrument plays them, where they sit in its range, and how many players carry them.
widgets.reuse_note: Works from standard orchestral ranges, not from a set work.

widgets.name: Trend, season or noise?
widgets.targets: A time series graph's overall trend must be distinguished from short-term seasonal fluctuations or noise, so a single rise doesn't confirm a rising trend
widgets.teaches: Separating the underlying trend of a time series from repeating seasonal variation and irregular noise, and what a 4-point moving average is for.

widgets.name: Across the core
widgets.targets: A transformer that steps up voltage causes current to decrease proportionally, so power (and total energy) is conserved, not increased.
widgets.teaches: A transformer that steps voltage up forces the current down by the same factor, because the power delivered can never exceed the power supplied.

widgets.name: Base current, collector current
widgets.targets: A transistor uses a small base/gate current to actively control a much larger collector/drain current, unlike a simple mechanical on/off switch.
widgets.teaches: A small base current controls a much larger collector current that the supply provides; below about 0.7 V the transistor is off, and above saturation the load sets the ceiling.

widgets.name: One God, three persons
widgets.targets: The Trinity is three co-eternal, simultaneously existing persons in one God, not three separate gods or one god wearing different masks in turn.
widgets.teaches: The Trinity as Christians state it: one God in three co-equal, co-eternal persons - not three gods (tritheism) and not one God in three modes (modalism).

wired_lessons.after: Creation: The World as God’s Gift
Why the Trinity Matters in Practice
Unitarians and Rejection of the Trinity

widgets.name: Give the order
widgets.targets: Ramming tactics at Salamis required precise coordinated timing, turning and repositioning, not a static head-on charge.
widgets.teaches: Ramming at Salamis was a coordinated manoeuvre needing sea room, not a head-on charge; the narrow strait denied the larger Persian fleet the room its numbers needed.
widgets.reuse_note: The geometry is the strait at Salamis. Only fits that battle.

widgets.name: Where the boundary Vs
widgets.targets: A downstream-dipping stratum produces an upstream-pointing V on a map because of the 3D geometry of a tilted bed intersecting a valley — the rule is a geometric consequence, not arbitrary.
widgets.teaches: A boundary crops out where the height of the bed matches the height of the ground, so its V in a valley points the way the bed dips; horizontal beds follow the contours and vertical beds cross straight.

widgets.name: Which kind of integration?
widgets.targets: Vertical integration moves along the supply chain (different stage), while horizontal integration combines businesses at the same stage — they are not the same thing.
widgets.teaches: Vertical integration buys a firm at a different stage of the supply chain; horizontal integration buys one at the same stage, and each buys a different power.
widgets.reuse_note: Firms are named by what they do, never by brand, so it carries across boards.

widgets.name: Sensor position in a voltage divider
widgets.targets: Whether output voltage rises or falls as a sensor's quantity increases depends on whether the sensor is the top or bottom resistor in the divider.
widgets.teaches: Whether V_out rises or falls as a sensed quantity changes depends on whether the sensor is R1 (above the tap) or R2 (below it).

widgets.name: Obeyed — but on what grounds?
widgets.targets: Traditional, charismatic and rational-legal authority differ in WHY people obey (the source of legitimacy), not in personality traits of the leader
widgets.teaches: Weber’s three types of authority differ in the source of legitimacy — why people accept the right to be obeyed — not in the leader’s personality.

wired_lessons.after: Formal and Informal Sources of Power

widgets.name: What the witches actually said
widgets.targets: The witches' statements are deliberately ambiguous, containing loopholes Macbeth fails to notice, rather than guaranteed truths that simply come to pass.
widgets.teaches: The prophecies are equivocations — every word true, every word shaped so Macbeth hears a guarantee. The loopholes are in the wording, and the false reading is his.
widgets.reuse_note: Macbeth's prophecies verbatim. Only fits a Macbeth lesson.

wired_lessons.after: False Confidence and the Turn to Tyranny

widgets.name: Zener regulator: move the supply
widgets.targets: A zener regulator actively clamps the output voltage constant despite rising input voltage, rather than passively behaving like a resistor.
widgets.teaches: A zener regulator holds V_out at V_Z by changing its own current; the supply and the series resistor set that current, not the output voltage.
